scope: continuous multi-objective minimization; all 43 requested catalogue families have callable members; see explicit member exclusions and version notes

suites.name: ZDT
suites.reference: Zitzler, Deb and Thiele (2000). Comparison of multiobjective evolutionary algorithms: Empirical results. DOI: 10.1162/106365600568202.
suites.notes: Real-valued ZDT1/2/3/4/6 only. Binary ZDT5 is excluded. Fractional powers require care at the decision-box boundary.

suites.name: DTLZ
suites.reference: Deb, Thiele, Laumanns and Zitzler (2002/2005). Scalable multiobjective optimization test problems; expanded chapter DOI: 10.1007/1-84628-137-7_6.
suites.notes: DTLZ1-7 only. DTLZ8 and DTLZ9 have explicit constraints and must not be added to this unconstrained branch.

suites.name: SCH
suites.reference: Schaffer (1985). Multiple objective optimization with vector evaluated genetic algorithms.
suites.notes: Schaffer N.1; this repository fixes the conventional [-1000, 1000] box. Other libraries sometimes use [-10, 10].

suites.name: FON
suites.reference: Fonseca and Fleming (1993). Genetic algorithms for multiobjective optimization: Formulation, discussion and generalization.
suites.notes: Scalable Fonseca-Fleming variant with 3 variables by default (called Fonseca2 in MOEA Framework).

suites.name: POL
suites.reference: Poloni, C. et al. (1996). Multiobjective Optimization by GAs: Application to System and Component Design. Computational Methods in Applied Sciences 96, 258-264. Corrected definition: Van Veldhuizen, D. A. (1999), Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithms: Classifications, Analyses, and New Innovations, PhD thesis, Appendix B.
suites.notes: Corrected Van Veldhuizen / MOEA Framework variant; positive objectives minimized here equal maximizing their negatives in MOEA Framework.

suites.name: WFG
suites.reference: Huband, S., Hingston, P., Barone, L. and While, L. (2006). A review of multiobjective test problems and a scalable test problem toolkit. IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 10(5), 477-506. DOI: 10.1109/TEVC.2005.861417.
suites.notes: Scalable objectives; k divisible by M-1, n_var>k, even distance count for WFG2/3. Defaults M=3, k=4, n_var=24. No analytical front sampler yet.

suites.name: IDTLZ
suites.reference: H. Jain and K. Deb. An evolutionary many-objective optimization algorithm using reference-point based non-dominated sorting approach, part II: Handling constraints and extending to an adaptive approach. IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, 2014, 18(4): 602-622.
suites.notes: Inverted DTLZ1/2: subtract each base objective from its common radial factor.

suites.name: SDTLZ
suites.reference: K. Deb and H. Jain. An evolutionary many-objective optimization algorithm using reference-point based non-dominated sorting approach, part I: Solving problems with box constraints. IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, 2014, 18(4): 577-601.
suites.notes: Scaled DTLZ1/2: multiply objective i by scale**i (zero-based); default scale=2.

suites.name: UF
suites.reference: Zhang et al. (2009). Multiobjective optimization test instances for the CEC 2009 special session and competition.
suites.notes: CEC 2009 UF1-10. Defaults n=30; UF1-7 have 2 objectives and n>=3, UF8-10 have 3 objectives and n>=5. UF5: N=10, epsilon=0.1; UF6: N=2, epsilon=0.1; UF9: epsilon=0.1.

suites.name: LZ09
suites.reference: Li and Zhang (2009). Multiobjective optimization problems with complicated Pareto sets, MOEA/D and NSGA-II.
suites.notes: jMetal LZ09_F1-9 numbering and unit decision box; internal transformations define the linked Pareto set.

suites.name: IMOP
suites.reference: Y. Tian, R. Cheng, X. Zhang, M. Li, and Y. Jin. Diversity assessment of multi-objective evolutionary algorithms: Performance metric and benchmark problems. IEEE Computational Intelligence Magazine, 2019, 14(3): 61-74.
suites.notes: IMOP1-8, including irregular and disconnected fronts; alpha1=0.05, alpha2=10, k=5 by default.

suites.name: MaF
suites.reference: R. Cheng, M. Li, Y. Tian, X. Zhang, S. Yang, Y. Jin, and X. Yao. A benchmark test suite for evolutionary many-objective optimization. Complex & Intelligent Systems, 2017, 3(1): 67-81. DOI: 10.1007/s40747-017-0039-7.
suites.notes: MaF1-15. MaF10 uses continuous WFG1 without the four-decimal b_flat rounding found in pinned PlatEMO. MaF9 rejects excluded polygons instead of randomly repairing inputs.

suites.name: ZCAT
suites.reference: Zapotecas-Martinez, S., Coello Coello, C. A., Aguirre, H. and Tanaka, K. (2023). Challenging test problems for multi- and many-objective optimization. Swarm and Evolutionary Computation 81, 101350. DOI: 10.1016/j.swevo.2023.101350.
suites.notes: ZCAT1-20 follow pinned jMetalPy (theta denominator n-p, not PlatEMO n). Default n=2*m, m=3; level, bias, imbalance and complicated_pareto_set are explicit constructor parameters.

suites.name: LSMOP
suites.reference: R. Cheng, Y. Jin, M. Olhofer, and B. Sendhoff. Test problems for large-scale multiobjective and many-objective optimization. IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics, 2017, 47(12): 4108-4121. DOI: 10.1109/TCYB.2016.2600577.
suites.notes: LSMOP1-9 with logistic grouping and scalable objectives/variables. Rejects dimensions yielding blocks shorter than two variables.

suites.name: MMF
suites.reference: C. Yue, B. Qu, and J. Liang. A multi-objective particle swarm optimizer using ring topology for solving multimodal multiobjective problems. IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, 2018, 22(5): 805-817.
suites.notes: MMF1-8, fixed two-variable definitions; piecewise transforms and absolute values are retained.

suites.name: Omni-test
suites.reference: Deb and Tiwari (2008). Omni-optimizer: A generic evolutionary algorithm for single and multi-objective optimization. Variant: pymoo 0.6.2 OmniTest.
suites.notes: OmniTest convention in pymoo 0.6.2: box [0,6]^n and 3^n equivalent Pareto subsets. The front sampler returns objective points, not decision-space subsets.

suites.name: SYM-PART
suites.reference: Rudolph, Naujoks and Preuss (2007). Capabilities of EMOA to Detect and Preserve Equivalent Pareto Subsets. Simple/rotated variants: pymoo 0.6.2.
suites.notes: Simple and rotated variants only; a=1, b=c=10, box [-100,100]^2, default rotation pi/4. Nine equivalent Pareto subsets. Rotated-distorted SYM-PART is excluded.

suites.name: FDA
suites.reference: M. Farina, K. Deb, and P. Amato. Dynamic multiobjective optimization problems: Test cases, approximations, and applications. IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, 2004, 8(5): 425-442.
suites.notes: FDA1-5 at explicit time=0 by default; at_time(t) creates a new fixed-time problem. FDA2 uses the corrected PlatEMO exponent. Time is not advanced by evaluations.

suites.name: JY
suites.reference: Jiang, S. and Yang, S. (2017). Evolutionary Dynamic Multiobjective Optimization: Benchmarks and Algorithm Comparisons. IEEE Transactions on Cybernetics 47(1), 198-211. DOI: 10.1109/TCYB.2015.2510698.
suites.notes: JY1-8, original October 2016 author JY.h with unit-box tail mapping 2*x-1. JY3 follows that file, not later RJY3 variants. JY8 restores its missing pow call (also confirmed by author-coauthored RJY8.m). Time is explicit.

suites.name: RE_continuous
suites.reference: Tanabe, R. and Ishibuchi, H. (2020). An easy-to-use real-world multi-objective optimization problem suite. Applied Soft Computing 89, 106078. DOI: 10.1016/j.asoc.2020.106078.
suites.notes: Ten deterministic, real-variable RE problems; discrete/rounded RE22/23/25/35/36 and stochastic RE91 are excluded. Positive-part violation objectives remain part of F.

suites.name: RWA
suites.reference: Zapotecas-Martinez, S., Garcia-Najera, A. and Menchaca-Mendez, A. (2023). Engineering applications of multi-objective evolutionary algorithms: A test suite of box-constrained real-world problems. Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence 123, 106192. DOI: 10.1016/j.engappai.2023.106192.
suites.notes: RWA1-10, pinned jMetalPy application mappings. Maximization objectives are negated, with application labels and signs recorded per problem.

suites.name: BNH
suites.reference: Binh and Korn (1997). MOBES: A multiobjective evolution strategy for constrained optimization problems.
suites.notes: Raw constraints; pymoo divides their residuals by 25 and 7.7.

suites.name: TNK
suites.reference: Tanaka et al. (1995). GA-based decision support system for multicriteria optimization.
suites.notes: Uses atan2(x1, x2); at the infeasible origin the angle is defined as zero. Raw second constraint has half the scale of pymoo.

suites.name: OSY
suites.reference: Osyczka and Kundu (1995). A new method to solve generalized multicriteria optimization problems using the simple genetic algorithm.
suites.notes: Raw residuals, with the first objective negative. See the explicit sign and scaling cross-checks.

suites.name: SRN
suites.reference: Srinivas and Deb (1994). Multiobjective optimization using nondominated sorting in genetic algorithms.
suites.notes: Two decision variables and two raw inequality constraints.

suites.name: CTP
suites.reference: Deb, K., Pratap, A. and Meyarivan, T. (2001). Constrained Test Problems for Multi-objective Evolutionary Optimization. EMO 2001, LNCS 1993, 284-298. DOI: 10.1007/3-540-44719-9_20.
suites.notes: CTP1-8 use signed unnormalized constraints. Default distance is linear; distance="multimodal" selects the alternative distance function. CTP1 supports multiple exponential constraints.

suites.name: CF
suites.reference: Zhang et al. (2009). Multiobjective optimization test instances for the CEC 2009 special session and competition.
suites.notes: CF1-10, signed constraints from the CEC 2009 reference. CF8-10 have a genuine singular constraint denominator at f3**2=1; no epsilon substitution is made.

suites.name: C-DTLZ
suites.reference: Jain and Deb (2014). NSGA-III, Part II: Handling constraints and extending to an adaptive approach.
suites.notes: Five named C1/C2/C3 variants; all default to M=3, n=M+9. Raw G<=0. Objective-dependent radii follow pymoo 0.6.2. Unconstrained DTLZ fronts are not returned as constrained fronts.

suites.name: DC-DTLZ
suites.reference: K. Li, R. Chen, G. Fu, and X. Yao. Two-archive evolutionary algorithm for constrained multi-objective optimization. IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, 2019, 23(2): 303-315. DOI: 10.1109/TEVC.2018.2855411.
suites.notes: DC1/2/3-DTLZ1 and DC1/2/3-DTLZ3. Pinned PlatEMO uses a distance coefficient of 10 in the DTLZ3 variants.

suites.name: Eq-DTLZ
suites.reference: Cuate, O., Uribe, L., Lara, A. and Schuetze, O. (2020). A benchmark for equality constrained multi-objective optimization. Swarm and Evolutionary Computation 52, 100619. DOI: 10.1016/j.swevo.2019.100619.
suites.notes: EqDTLZ1-4, n_equalities=1 or 2. Returns signed sphere residuals in H; the author supplement encodes abs(H)-1e-4 as inequalities. Feasibility tolerance is selected at evaluation time.

suites.name: Eq-IDTLZ
suites.reference: Cuate, O., Uribe, L., Lara, A. and Schuetze, O. (2020). A benchmark for equality constrained multi-objective optimization. Swarm and Evolutionary Computation 52, 100619. DOI: 10.1016/j.swevo.2019.100619.
suites.notes: EqIDTLZ1/2 with one or two sphere equalities, using the same signed-H convention as Eq-DTLZ.

suites.name: MW
suites.reference: Z. Ma and Y. Wang. Evolutionary constrained multiobjective optimization: Test suite construction and performance comparisons. IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, 2019, 23(6): 972-986.
suites.notes: MW1-14 follow pymoo 0.6.2. Published implementations differ in MW4/6/11/12/13/14; do not mix reference fronts or boxes from other versions.

suites.name: LIR-CMOP
suites.reference: Z. Fan, W. Li, X. Cai, H. Huang, Y. Fang, Y. You, J. Mo, C. Wei, and E. Goodman. An improved epsilon constraint-handling method in MOEA/D for CMOPs with large infeasible regions. Soft Computing, 2019, 23: 12491-12510.
suites.notes: LIRCMOP1-14 follow pinned PlatEMO, including its LIRCMOP2-4 tail shift and LIRCMOP13/14 radial offset.

suites.name: DAS-CMOP
suites.reference: Z. Fan, W. Li, X. Cai, H. Li, C. Wei, Q. Zhang, K. Deb, and E. Goodman. Difficulty adjustable and scalable constrained multi-objective test problem toolkit. Evolutionary Computation, 2020, 28(3): 339-378.
suites.notes: DASCMOP1-9, difficulty presets 1-16 or explicit (eta,zeta,gamma). Uses pymoo 0.6.2 tail-only g for 1-3, which differs from the PlatEMO all-variable sum. Disabled constraints stay nonpositive.

suites.name: DAS-CMaOP
suites.reference: Z. Fan, W. Li, X. Cai, H. Li, C. Wei, Q. Zhang, K. Deb, and E. Goodman. Difficulty adjustable and scalable constrained multi-objective test problem toolkit. Evolutionary Computation, 2020, 28(3): 339-378.
suites.notes: DASCMaOP1-9 use WFG1-9 transformations and Fan et al. equation (8). Difficulty presets 1-12 or (eta,zeta,gamma); default k=2*(m-1) satisfies WFG grouping divisibility.

suites.name: DOC
suites.reference: Z. Liu and Y. Wang. Handling constrained multiobjective optimization problems with constraints in both the decision and objective spaces. IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, 2019, 23(5): 870-884.
suites.notes: DOC1-9 retain original equality bands abs(h)-1e-4 as G inequalities, but remove positive-part clipping and batch normalization from raw constraint residuals.

suites.name: NCTP
suites.reference: Li, J.-P., Wang, Y., Yang, S. and Cai, Z. (2016). A comparative study of constraint-handling techniques in evolutionary constrained multiobjective optimization. IEEE CEC, 4175-4182. DOI: 10.1109/CEC.2016.7744320.
suites.notes: NCTP1-6 map to type I, 7-12 to type II, 13-18 to type III, each local member 1-6 in the author archive. Original bounds are [0,5] for every variable. Raw G removes positive-part clipping and population-dependent normalization.

suites.name: ZXH_CF
suites.reference: Y. Zhou, Y. Xiang, and X. He. Constrained multiobjective optimization: Test problem construction and performance evaluations. IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation, 2021, 25(1): 172-186.
suites.notes: ZXH_CF1-16, pinned PlatEMO definitions, box [1e-10,1-1e-10].

suites.name: LSCMOP
suites.reference: Qiao, K., Liang, J., Yu, K., Guo, W., Yue, C., Qu, B. and Suganthan, P. N. (2024). Benchmark problems for large-scale constrained multi-objective optimization with baseline results. Swarm and Evolutionary Computation 86, 101504. DOI: 10.1016/j.swevo.2024.101504.
suites.notes: LSCMOP1-12 are the author LSCM1-12. Preserves the aggregate positive constraint violation and numerical cutoffs; its constraint Jacobian is zero in feasible interiors. No implicit dimension rounding.

suites.name: CMMOP
suites.reference: Ming, F., Gong, W., Yang, Y. and Liao, Z. (2023). Constrained multimodal multi-objective optimization: Test problem construction and algorithm design. Swarm and Evolutionary Computation 76, 101209. DOI: 10.1016/j.swevo.2022.101209.
suites.notes: CMMOP1-14 follow the author archive. Preserves conditional feasible-region constraints, including the zero second column in CMMOP8.

suites.name: CRE
suites.reference: Tanabe, R. and Ishibuchi, H. (2020). An easy-to-use real-world multi-objective optimization problem suite. Applied Soft Computing 89, 106078. DOI: 10.1016/j.asoc.2020.106078.
suites.notes: CRE21/22/23/31/32/51. Returns raw signed G (feasible <=0), while the original code returns clipped violations. Discrete CRE24/25 are excluded.

suites.name: Welded-Beam
suites.reference: Deb, K., Sundar, J., Rao, N. U. B. and Chaudhuri, S. (2006). Reference Point Based Multi-Objective Optimization Using Evolutionary Algorithms. International Journal of Computational Intelligence Research 2(3), 273-286.
suites.notes: Two objectives and four raw constraints, matching pymoo 0.6.2. J uses sqrt(2)*h*l*(l^2/12+(h+t)^2/4), which differs from variants using twice this J. Variables (h,l,t,b) in inches. See formula constants and raw residual scaling.

suites.name: RCM_continuous
suites.reference: Kumar, A., Wu, G., Ali, M. Z., Luo, Q., Mallipeddi, R., Suganthan, P. N. and Das, S. (2021). A Benchmark-Suite of real-World constrained multi-objective optimization problems and some baseline results. Swarm and Evolutionary Computation 67, 100961. DOI: 10.1016/j.swevo.2021.100961.
suites.notes: 39 continuous author-code definitions from RCM2-50, preserving original numbering. RCM5/14 are continuous relaxations of disk counts. Excludes integer/rounded problems 1/6/7/13/15/19/25-29. RCM9 has no effective constraint. RCM50 fixes batch-dependent P(j) to rowwise quadratic loss.
